review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some argue that based on academic performance, students who shows the most outstanding results should be rewarded accordingly by school council. Others, however, believed that praised and rewarded the group of students show their advancement is much more necessary. From my perspective, there are strong evidences for both sides of the argument.

Admittedly, rewarding to students who express themselves with the excellent results in school is, without any doubt, essential and obvious. Indeed, students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies, obviously, they deserved their acknowledgements and privileges. Following that, this may encourage and others to study harder to win the rewards, thus propelling the overall academic gains. Moreover, this will naturally create competition between students and this kind of competition can be easily seen in almost every aspects of life, where only the most superior student are rewarded. Students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition. In this way, academic competition can deeply help students develop their determination and how to deal with academic pressure.

On the other hand, rewarding students who show their improvement can also have some huge benefit. If only a few smart student can come first and receive the rewards, this may cause others to think their efforts are futile because they can not surpass those high achieving individuals. As a results, they may be prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, and then gradually lose the purpose and incentive to study. Therefore, emphasizing improvement has a crucial role in encouraging all students to be dedicated in their studies. This also helps student to constantly improve themselves, regardless how well they have been or are performing. This constant desire to better themselves can even benefit them more than determination to overcome to win against all others.
In conclusion, both approaches have their own benefits. Therefore, I strongly believe schools should reward both high achievement and significant improvement.

completion.comment: Em đã viết đủ mở bài, hai thân bài và kết luận.

review.overall: Em viết đủ hai quan điểm và kết luận rõ nên thưởng cả thành tích cao lẫn sự tiến bộ. Body 1 có ý về công sức và việc làm quen với cạnh tranh; Body 2 nối được cảm giác nản chí với động lực tự cải thiện. Tuy nhiên, nhiều câu ghép khung sai ngay ở mở bài và thân bài như 'students who shows', 'believed that praised and rewarded' và 'rewarding to students'; việc tự soát ngữ pháp của bài này còn cẩu thả. Em cần viết lại từng câu theo chủ ngữ–động từ rõ, đọc kỹ từng chú thích rồi tự đối chiếu bản sửa, thay vì chỉ thay vài từ rời. Body 1 có “Moreover” đúng cho lý do cạnh tranh nhưng “Indeed” chỉ nhấn mạnh, chưa báo lý do công sức là nhánh đầu. Body 2 vào thẳng điều kiện “If only...” rồi dùng “Therefore” cho ích lợi tiến bộ, làm lý do thứ hai giống hệ quả của sự nản chí; bản cũ đã chấm chuyển ý Đạt nên cần sửa.

In this way, academic competition can deeply help students develop their determination and learn how to deal with academic pressure.

Supporters of rewarding improvement, however, argue that rewarding students who show improvement can also have significant benefits. The first reason is that if only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, this may cause others to think their efforts are futile. This is because they may feel unable to surpass those high-achieving individuals. As a result, they may be prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, and then gradually lose the purpose and incentive to study. Furthermore, emphasizing improvement has a crucial role in encouraging all students to be dedicated in their studies. This also helps students to constantly improve themselves, regardless of how well they have been or are performing. This constant desire to better themselves can even benefit them more than the determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, both approaches have their own benefits. Therefore, I strongly believe schools should reward both high achievement and significant improvement.
